originalTitle: Australia politics live: impassioned Lambie accuses Labor of ‘callous disregard’ for veterans’ health; Steggall urges action on domestic violence deaths
content: ‘Time for young workers to be paid the super they deserve’: Greens push for super for under 18s Over on the other side of Parliament, Greens senator Barbara Pocock is pushing for kids under the age of 18 to be paid compulsory superannuation. Right now, workers under 18 only get guaranteed super payments if they work more than 30 hours. The Greens have a private members bill, and despite the Labor national platform endorsing an amendment to give under 18s compulsory super, it’s pretty unlikely the government will support this legislation, because … well … politics. Pocock tells the chamber: It’s time for young workers to be paid the super, they deserve. In practice, what’s going on right now is that hundreds of thousands of young Australians who are under at the age of 18 are missing out, and every year, 530,000 young teenage workers are denied the astonishing sum of $411m in super for no reason other than their age … Yet many of them are denied compulsory superannuation contributions simply because of their age. Hundreds of thousands of young workers are being held back financially before they’ve even had a chance to get ahead. Independent MP Zali Steggall has moved to suspend proceedings in the lower house over the dozens of deaths of women and children in Australia killed by domestic and family violence, and urge the government to acknowledge that it remains a national crisis despite efforts. Her motion states that Australian Femicide Watch has recorded 45 women and 19 children killed by violence this year. She tells the house the government should call a royal commission into femicide and domestic and family violence, establish a domestic violence offender register and address recommendations from previous reviews that have been ignored or not acted on. This motion calls on the government to act with urgency on so many issues that remain outstanding, too many inquiries, have urgent recommendations that have not been actioned, and there is no real rational explanation as to why that has not occurred to date. Much, much work must be done in this space by the government, including establish things like a DV offender register and for national actions. We need to get to a process of elevating this issue, to ensure women and girls are safe. These numbers are unacceptable. The minister for social services, Tanya Plibersek, thanks Steggall for bringing the motion forward and says commonwealth, state and territory governments “must be held to account for our progress on ending family, domestic and sexual violence in Australia.” The member has called for a royal commission. And I understand that this call comes from a very good place … But Mr Speaker, we don’t need another report. As the members themselves have said, last year’s domestic family and sexual violence commissioner’s annual report to parliament pointed out that we have 1000 recommendations already from a variety of reports across eight royal commissions, eight major reports like royal commissions, inquiries, and reviews to guide us … The South Australian royal commission [into domestic, family and sexual violence] took 17 months from its beginning to its end. I don’t want to spend another 17 months examining the same issue that we’ve examined in eight major reports recently. We need to get on and act. Six months ago, Jacqui Lambie says her vagina started to prolapse, and three months ago it took her “bladder with it”. She says this is directly connected to her military service. Yesterday in a fiery and emotional speech in the chamber, the Tasmanian independent senator detailed her story of battling with health access as a defence veteran, begging the government to scrap a controversial $5,000 cap on allied health services for veterans. She accused the government of a “callous disregard for veterans’ health and wellbeing”. On Tuesday night, Lambie had told the story of how it took female veteran Kate three years to get surgery for vaginal prolapse because “she couldn’t find a gynaecologist who was happy with the low prices [the Department of Veterans’ Affairs] pay”. On Wednesday, Lambie said she had travelled to the mainland and paid $7,000 to avoid the same fate as Kate. “That’s how much they care about our vaginas,” Lambie said. Vaginal prolapse is a condition suffered by one in 12 Australian women, but there is no accurate data, Lambie said. She quoted a survey of nearly 500 female veterans who had completed a minimum of six months’ active duty that found two-thirds reported pelvic health concerns, including 12% who reported pelvic organ collapse. I would like to ask the prime minister, minister [Richard] Marles and minister [Matt] Keogh what they would do if their penises were hanging by a thread, and what would they do if treatment for that injury directly connected to their military service was denied by the Department of Veterans’ Affairs. Would they say, ‘OK, no worries. I don’t really need my penis’? I don’t think so. I’m begging you, prime minister. We are already suffering enough. Drop the bloody cap. Drop it, mate. It is so unfair. It is what we do not need. It is enough. Veterans have had enough. Leave us alone. Initial language around sexual assault allegations ‘unfortunate’, says minister The emergency services minister, Kristy McBain said some of the language used around an alleged sexual assault in Melbourne in the early hours of Monday morning shows “we still have a long way to go” to fix the culture. Five Sydney Swans players were banned for the rest of the season on Wednesday for breaching club standards, in relation to their behaviour on a night out. Separately, Victoria police have also said they are investigating an alleged sexual assault at the Pullman Hotel near the MCG. None of the players have been arrested or charged with any offences. chineseTitle: 澳大利亚政治现场：慷慨激昂的兰比指责工党“无情地漠视”退伍军人的健康；斯蒂格尔敦促对家庭暴力死亡采取行动
chineseContent: “是时候让年轻工人获得应得的养老金了”：绿党推动为 18 岁以下的儿童支付养老金 在议会的另一边，绿党参议员芭芭拉·波考克 (Barbara Pocock) 正在推动向 18 岁以下的儿童支付强制性养老金。目前，18 岁以下的工人只有工作超过 30 小时才能获得有保障的养老金。绿党有一项私人议员法案，尽管工党全国政纲支持一项修正案，给予 18 岁以下的强制退休金，但政府不太可能支持这项立法，因为……嗯……政治。波科克告诉商会：现在是年轻工人获得退休金的时候了，他们应得的。实际上，现在的情况是，数十万18岁以下的澳大利亚年轻人被错过了，每年有53万名青少年工人因为年龄而被拒绝领取高达4.11亿美元的惊人养老金……然而，他们中的许多人仅仅因为年龄而被拒绝缴纳强制性养老金。数十万年轻工人在有机会获得成功之前就受到了经济上的阻碍。独立议员扎利·斯特格尔已采取行动，暂停下议院对澳大利亚数十名妇女和儿童因家庭暴力而死亡的诉讼，并敦促政府承认，尽管做出了努力，这仍然是一场全国危机。她的动议指出，澳大利亚杀戮女性观察组织今年已记录了 45 名妇女和 19 名儿童死于暴力事件。她告诉众议院，政府应该召集皇家委员会调查杀害女性和家庭暴力问题，建立家庭暴力犯罪者登记册，并解决之前审查中被忽视或未采取行动的建议。这项议案
